description: Thin arrows keep a sensor alert population live as its threshold changes
code:
class Sensor(code: str, level: int):
    this.code = code
    this.level = level
Sensor("A", 3); Sensor("B", 8); Sensor("C", 12)
threshold = 5
alerts = Sensor.filter(sensor -> sensor.level > threshold)
codes = alerts.map((sensor) -> sensor.code)
assert(codes, ["B", "C"])
threshold = 10
assert(codes, ["C"])
Sensor("D", 15)
assert(codes, ["C", "D"])
codes

description: Python style lambdas map and total live order lines
code:
tax = 0.5
prices = [10, 20]
taxed = prices.map(lambda price: price + price * tax)
total = taxed.reduce(lambda sum, price: sum + price, 0)
assert(taxed, [15, 30])
assert(total, 45)
tax = 0
assert(total, 30)
prices.push(5)
assert(total, 35)
total

description: Thin arrow named functions cover bare typed comma-free and indented headers
code:
rate = 2
def fee amount -> amount * rate
def capped amount: int, limit: int -> Math.min(amount * rate, limit)
def label code name -> `${code}:${name}`
def doubled value ->
    value * 2
charge = fee(10)
assert(charge, 20)
assert(capped(10, 15), 15)
assert(label("A", "pump"), "A:pump")
assert(doubled(charge), 40)
rate = 3
assert(charge, 30)
charge

description: A variable named lambda keeps its slice header and comma-free property readings
code:
lambda = 1
items = ["a", "b", "c"]
tail = items[lambda:]
record = { head: lambda next: 2 }
if lambda:
    mode = "on"
square = lambda -> lambda * lambda
assert(tail, ["b", "c"])
assert([record.head, record.next], [1, 2])
assert(mode, "on")
assert(square(3), 9)
lambda = 2
assert(tail, ["c"])
tail
